A public_note ships. (4b) WORDING OF THE FOURTH ITEM: 'I think about where I am today' is the one shipped sentence that is NOT in the Italian validation's Table 9, because the TFS-I dropped it. STEP 3b RESOLVED DECISIVELY -- the scale is identified, not guessed. The paper's Procedure & measures says "We used the Deployment Concerns subscale of the Deployment Risk and Resiliency Inventory-2 (DRRI-2 [44])... 12 items... (e.g., 'I thought I would never survive.'; 1-Strongly Disagree, 5-Strongly Agree; Cronbach's alpha = .90)". The NCPTSD scale page https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/deployment/perceived-threat.asp (read 2026-09-20, page sha256 156f72547f36348eed1af71dabf2b97ef250fd21b689d14c8bd73387f82c2ff4) names it 'Perceived Threat Scale', 'DRRI-2 Section: G', 'Survey Label: "Deployment Concerns"', 5-point Likert 1=Strongly disagree to 5=Strongly agree, and prints as its Sample Item the exact sentence carried by drri5. The authoritative DRRI-2 Scales form (https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/documents/DRRI2scales.pdf, sha256 5b17c1bfb66ccbd105163d65509a178c83f41e6c907e6da2916a06b6df69080e) prints Section G as exactly 12 numbered items in exactly the order drri1..drri12 carry, so both the count and the numbering line up item for item. This is the DRRI-2 Perceived Threat / Deployment Concerns scale, not the Post-Deployment Social Support subscale that the same deposit's social1-social15 columns hold (that is the separate, still-queued wesselmann_2018_social_support table). (1) ITEM TEXT IS THE .sav's OWN VARIABLE LABELS, VERBATIM, corroborated by the authors' codebook. data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts the PLOS S1 File (.sav) on the literal column list [f'drri{i}' for i in range(1,13)], so the IRW item code IS the source column name (derivation pattern 1); item_text is those 12 SPSS variable labels transcribed character for character (12/12 exact string equality, checked programmatically; longest label 111 chars, far under the 255 SPSS cap, so none is truncated). The authors' OSF codebook (https://osf.io/enp9g/download, sha256 b3e1ee71d817f05ec4902a6321cbaa9498537a31041dfa135059152acc358a9c) lists the same 12 codes against the same 12 sentences under the heading 'Combat stressors (DRRI-2; Vogt, Smith, King, King, Knight, & Vasterling, 2013)'. Against the canonical DRRI-2 form, 11 of 12 are character-identical and drri2 differs only by the study dropping the sentence-final period after '(NBC) agents'; the study's wording was shipped and was NOT normalised. The form also prefixes every Section G item with a shared column stem 'During deployment...' and a leading ellipsis ('...I was concerned about getting an infectious disease.'); neither the .sav labels nor the codebook reproduces that, so it was NOT added to item_text or to section_prompt. (2) INSTRUCTIONS ARE THE STUDY'S OWN PROMPT, which happens to be the form's verbatim Section G instruction. The codebook prints 'The statements below are about the amount of danger you felt you were exposed to during your most recent deployment. Please mark how much you agree or disagree with each statement.' and lines 372-373 of the DRRI-2 Scales PDF print the identical sentence above Section G. (Note this is the same prompt the codebook ALSO misprints under its PCL-5 heading, which batch_223 diagnosed as a copy-paste error -- here it is in its correct place.) (3) THE FIVE ANCHORS COME FROM THE DRRI-2 FORM, BECAUSE THE STUDY'S OWN PRINTING IS GARBLED. The .sav carries no value labels at all (pyreadstat variable_value_labels is empty for every variable in the file), and the codebook's line reads '[Rating Scale: Strongly Agree, Somewhat Disagree, Neither Agree nor Disagree; Somewhat Agree, Strongly Agree]' -- position 1 is a transcription error for 'Strongly Disagree' (it duplicates position 5, and the paper states '1-Strongly Disagree, 5-Strongly Agree'). option_text therefore transcribes the DRRI-2 Scales PDF's own printed column headers, in the form's own sentence case: 1 Strongly disagree, 2 Somewhat disagree, 3 Neither agree nor disagree, 4 Somewhat agree, 5 Strongly agree. No scale point was padded with its own number, and none is blank. SCALE DIRECTION CHECKED AGAINST THE DATA, not assumed (N=128): the .sav's own 'concern' composite ('combat stressors (DRRI) average') equals the plain UNREVERSED mean of drri1..drri12 exactly (max |diff| = 0.000), while the reversed mean (6 - x) is off by up to 4.000, so no item is stored reverse-coded and the file ships no drri*R columns. That composite correlates +0.403 traitanx, +0.394 stateanx, +0.393 ptsd, +0.260 distress, +0.249 chronic ostracism and -0.179 support, -0.277 milsupport -- higher raw = more deployment concern, fixing 1 = Strongly disagree and 5 = Strongly agree as shipped. Cronbach's alpha computed from the raw 12 items is 0.902 (n=117 complete), reproducing the paper's reported .90. Content coherence agrees: the highest means are drri5 explosive device 3.38, drri11 locals working against us 3.27 and drri7 rocket/mortar 3.07, the lowest drri9 'I thought I would never survive' 1.74 and drri8 depleted uranium 1.99 -- the expected profile for a National Guard deployment sample.
